youtube.title: How Did AWS Become Amazon's Profit Machine?
youtube.description:
Amazon is a store, so why does most of its profit come from renting computers? In 2006 Amazon began selling storage and servers to outside developers by the hour. Business magazines called it a risky bet. By 2024 that unit, Amazon Web Services, earned $39.8 billion in operating profit, 58 percent of Amazon's total, from about 17 percent of its sales.

This documentary follows the decision from a 2003 executive retreat to the 2006 launch of S3 and EC2, the startups and the Netflix move that followed, the 2015 moment Amazon first showed AWS's numbers, and the year the stores lost $10.6 billion while AWS carried the company. It also tests the popular story that Amazon simply rented out spare servers, which Amazon's own CTO calls a myth.

{CHAPTERS}

youtube.comment: If you had to pick one product Amazon could never give up, would it be AWS, Prime or the store itself? 👇

sources.claim: Amazon launched S3 on March 14, 2006, promising developers the same storage infrastructure that ran Amazon's own websites
sources.source: Amazon press release, 'Amazon Web Services Launches Amazon S3', 14 Mar 2006

sources.claim: S3 cost fifteen cents per gigabyte per month with no minimum fee
sources.source: Amazon S3 launch press release and pricing page, 14 Mar 2006

sources.claim: EC2 launched in beta in August 2006; a small virtual server cost ten cents an hour
sources.source: Amazon press release announcing Amazon EC2 limited beta, 24 Aug 2006

sources.claim: A November 2006 BusinessWeek cover called the push Jeff Bezos's risky bet
sources.source: BusinessWeek cover story, 'Jeff Bezos' Risky Bet', Robert D. Hof, 13 Nov 2006

sources.claim: In 2024 AWS earned $39.8 billion in operating income on $107.6 billion of sales
sources.source: Amazon.com Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal 2024, segment information, filed Feb 2025

sources.claim: Amazon's total 2024 operating income was $68.6 billion and net sales $638.0 billion, so AWS was 58 percent of operating profit from about 17 percent of sales
sources.source: Amazon.com Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal 2024, filed Feb 2025 (percentages calculated from the filed figures)

sources.claim: Amazon was founded in 1994 and listed on Nasdaq in 1997
sources.source: Amazon.com Inc. IPO prospectus, May 1997

sources.claim: Amazon's first full-year profit came in 2003: net income of $35 million on sales of $5.26 billion
sources.source: Amazon.com Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal 2003, filed Feb 2004

sources.claim: Amazon's share price fell more than ninety percent between December 1999 and September 2001
sources.source: Nasdaq historical price data for AMZN, Dec 1999 to Sep 2001

sources.claim: Andy Jassy, then Bezos's technical assistant, said teams kept rebuilding the same infrastructure; a 2003 retreat at Bezos's house concluded Amazon had become good at running reliable, scalable infrastructure; a vision document came first
sources.source: Ron Miller, 'How AWS came to be', TechCrunch, 2 Jul 2016 (interview with Andy Jassy)

sources.claim: An early-2000s order said all teams will henceforth expose their data and functionality through service interfaces, and anyone who did not would be fired
sources.source: Steve Yegge, former Amazon engineer, public Google+ post recalling the memo, 12 Oct 2011 (one engineer's recollection)

sources.claim: Chris Pinkham and Benjamin Black wrote a 2003 paper on standardized, automated infrastructure that mentioned selling virtual servers as a service
sources.source: Benjamin Black, 'EC2 Origins', personal blog, 25 Jan 2009

sources.claim: EC2 was built by a team Chris Pinkham led in Cape Town, South Africa
sources.source: Benjamin Black, 'EC2 Origins', 25 Jan 2009; Ron Miller, TechCrunch, 2 Jul 2016

sources.claim: A message-queue service, SQS, opened to developers in beta in 2004
sources.source: Amazon Web Services blog announcement of Simple Queue Service beta, Nov 2004

sources.claim: Werner Vogels: it was never a matter of selling excess capacity; within two months of launch AWS would have burned through Amazon.com's excess capacity
sources.source: Werner Vogels, Amazon CTO, public answer on Quora, 2011

sources.claim: In April 2008 Animoto grew from about 50 servers to 3,500 in three days after going viral on Facebook
sources.source: Werner Vogels, 'Animoto - Scaling Through Viral Growth', All Things Distributed blog, Apr 2008

sources.claim: In August 2008 a database corruption stopped Netflix shipping DVDs for three days; it moved to AWS and finished in January 2016
sources.source: Yury Izrailevsky, 'Completing the Netflix Cloud Migration', Netflix blog, 11 Feb 2016

sources.claim: Google App Engine opened in preview in April 2008; Google Compute Engine in preview in June 2012
sources.source: Google official blog announcements, 7 Apr 2008 and 28 Jun 2012

sources.claim: Microsoft's Azure went live commercially in February 2010
sources.source: Microsoft press release on Windows Azure commercial availability, 1 Feb 2010

sources.claim: S3 held more than two trillion objects in 2013
sources.source: Jeff Barr, 'Amazon S3 - Two Trillion Objects', AWS News Blog, 18 Apr 2013

sources.claim: Before 2015 AWS results were included in Amazon's 'other' sales; Amazon first reported AWS separately in April 2015
sources.source: Amazon.com Inc. Q1 2015 earnings release, 23 Apr 2015; Form 10-K filings 2006-2014

sources.claim: AWS revenue was $4.6 billion in 2014 and operating income $265 million in Q1 2015
sources.source: Amazon.com Inc. Q1 2015 earnings release, 23 Apr 2015

sources.claim: Bezos wrote that AWS reached $10 billion in annual sales faster than Amazon itself reached that mark
sources.source: Jeff Bezos, 2015 Letter to Shareholders, Apr 2016
Amazon.com Inc. Form 10-K filings, fiscal 2016 through fiscal 2024, segment information

sources.claim: In 2017 AWS operating income was $4.33 billion against Amazon's total of $4.11 billion; the international segment lost $3.1 billion
sources.source: Amazon.com Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal 2017, filed Feb 2018

sources.claim: In 2022 AWS earned $22.8 billion operating income, Amazon $12.2 billion; North America lost $2.8 billion and International $7.7 billion, $10.6 billion together
sources.source: Amazon.com Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal 2022, filed Feb 2023

sources.claim: Amazon spent $83 billion on property and equipment in 2024, much of it for AWS
sources.source: Amazon.com Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal 2024 (cash capital expenditures); Andy Jassy, Q4 2024 earnings call, 6 Feb 2025

sources.claim: On February 28, 2017, a mistyped command took part of S3 offline in Northern Virginia for hours
sources.source: AWS, 'Summary of the Amazon S3 Service Disruption in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region', Mar 2017

sources.claim: Dropbox moved most of its storage onto its own machines and said this cut costs by $74.6 million over two years
sources.source: Dropbox Inc. Form S-1 registration statement, 23 Feb 2018

sources.claim: At the end of 2024 AWS held about 30 percent of cloud infrastructure, Microsoft about 21 percent
sources.source: Synergy Research Group, cloud infrastructure market share, Q4 2024 release, Feb 2025

sources.claim: Netflix, a Prime Video competitor, still runs on AWS
sources.source: Netflix Technology Blog, 11 Feb 2016; AWS customer case study, Netflix

sources.claim: Andy Jassy became Amazon's CEO on July 5, 2021, having run AWS since its start
sources.source: Amazon press release and Jeff Bezos letter to employees, 2 Feb 2021; Amazon announcement, 5 Jul 2021

sources.claim: Intel decided in 1985 to leave the memory-chip business
sources.source: Andrew S. Grove, 'Only the Paranoid Survive', Doubleday, 1996
